about.intro: I am a DePauw University Computer Science and Mathematics student building full-stack, mobile, blockchain, and AI systems with hands-on experience across React, React Native, FastAPI, Spring Boot, Oracle SQL, AWS, and automation workflows.
details: At Pay Your Tuition Foundation, I built Webflow, Memberstack, Salesforce, Make, Razorpay, JavaScript, REST API, and webhook workflows for a student crowdfunding and tuition-support platform serving 2,000+ students.
At VietinBank, I engineered Java Spring Boot, Oracle SQL, REST API, Python, and SQL data workflows for transaction validation, account lookup, reconciliation, dashboards, and reporting.
My project work includes ProofVault, KITES, AI agent workflows, computer vision, optimization, and interactive systems, with a practical bias toward products that are useful to real users.

projects.name: ProofVault
projects.summary: Full-stack evidence verification platform with blockchain-backed integrity checks, case-based file organization, SHA-256 fingerprints, Polygon proofs, and LLM-assisted review flows.
impact: Engineered a verification system with case-based file organization, hash generation, blockchain proof recording, and tamper detection.
Developed 11 FastAPI endpoints including presigned-upload and file-verification APIs with ownership validation, SQLAlchemy models, Alembic migrations, and transactional database operations.
Designed a Dockerized AWS architecture with private S3 storage, least-privilege IAM, ECR, ECS/Fargate, ALB health checks, CloudWatch logging, and Amplify deployment.

projects.name: KITES
projects.summary: Android family-safety app with role-based access, location tracking, guardian management, emergency communication, and Gemini-powered chatbot guidance.
impact: Built and deployed mobile functionality with React Native, Express.js backend services, React Native Maps, guardian management, and emergency communication.
Designed a modular TypeScript architecture with REST APIs, Recoil, AsyncStorage, and centralized service layers.
Supported 10+ parent-facing safety features while simplifying maintenance and debugging with Claude Code.

projects.name: Space Station Rescue Simulator
projects.summary: Built a basic pixel rescue game where players aim fuel cells ahead of a moving space station, manage a limited supply, and complete three increasingly fast deliveries. Includes a playable browser edition and a Java desktop edition.
impact: Built 3 rescue rounds and 3 difficulty settings on an 800 × 600 playfield, with keyboard and touch controls, pause/resume, restart, and optional fullscreen.
Implemented a 5-cell capacity, a 2-cell reward after successful deliveries, and round-weighted scoring with an 840-point maximum for three first-shot deliveries.
Verified the browser engine with 13 passing automated tests covering launch limits, movement bounds, pause/resume, collision detection, rewards, scoring, victory, loss, and restart.

projects.name: Tiger Cub
projects.summary: Interactive graphics project focused on animation, visual composition, and smooth object movement.
impact: Built a visual scene with animated elements and timing-based interaction.
Practiced graphics programming fundamentals including object drawing, transforms, and frame updates.
Designed the project as a polished visual demo with clear motion and presentation.

projects.name: Neural Network Character Recognition
projects.summary: Rebuilt a Java/BlueJ handwriting recognizer in Python and TensorFlow to identify handwritten digits 0–9. A colorful pixel-themed browser interface lets users draw with a mouse or touch, recognize the number, and clear the canvas; predictions run locally using a saved CNN model.
impact: Trained on 10,000 MNIST images, validated on 2,000 separate images, and evaluated on 10,000 held-out test images: 22,000 handwritten samples processed across disjoint splits.

Achieved 97.36% test accuracy (9,736 of 10,000 digits correct) and 96.95% validation accuracy after 5 epochs, exceeding the original 89% target by 8.36 percentage points. Test cross-entropy loss: 0.0843.

Created a shared image-processing pipeline for dataset images and user drawings: grayscale conversion, ink cropping, aspect-preserving resizing to 20×20, center-of-mass alignment on a 28×28 canvas, and normalization to [0, 1].
Built a CNN with 32- and 64-filter convolutional layers, max pooling, a 64-unit dense layer, 30% dropout, and a 10-class softmax output; trained with Adam using batches of 128 images.

Saved the model and evaluation report with per-epoch accuracy/loss, a 10×10 confusion matrix, and per-digit precision/recall. Passed 8 automated tests covering preprocessing, request validation, saved-model loading, and inference.
Accuracy was measured on unseen MNIST test digits; results on new mouse-drawn handwriting can vary. Training and detailed evaluation remain available through the Python command-line tooling.

projects.name: Solving Generalized Sudoku by Simulated Annealing
projects.summary: Optimization-based Sudoku solver exploring simulated annealing behavior, convergence, and search performance.
impact: Implemented a stochastic local-search solver using simulated annealing for Sudoku optimization.
Studied temperature schedules, candidate moves, and convergence behavior across puzzle states.
Documented the final method and results in an attached project paper.

projects.name: AI Chatbot
projects.summary: Browser-based chatbot with asynchronous Gemini calls, prompt handling, session state, loading feedback, and responsive chat UI.
impact: Implemented multi-turn message handling and context-aware session flow.
Designed loading, error, and response rendering states for a smoother chat experience.
Built the UI with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for direct browser portability.

projects.name: Avoid the Enemies
projects.summary: A full-window pixel-art survival game built with React and TypeScript. Players choose a character and dodge incoming enemies through three increasingly fast levels using keyboard, mouse, or touch controls.
impact: Implemented 3 playable avatars, 3 difficulty settings, and 3 levels with enemy speed increasing by 17% per level relative to the first level.
Made enemy counts configurable from 1 to 1,000 per level. The default 15-enemy setting requires 45 dodges across a complete run, with 100 points per enemy and a maximum default score of 4,500.
Separated the game engine from SVG rendering and React controls; verified collision boundaries, pause/resume, collision loss, three-level victory, and movement/reset with 5 automated tests.

Developed reporting APIs and reusable data-processing modules that delivered validated transaction and balance data to internal dashboards and monthly reports, reducing errors and accelerating issue investigation.

Identified recurring user problems and created reusable troubleshooting guidance and documentation, helping improve support consistency while managing multiple requests with a strong focus on urgency, accuracy, and user experience.

Worked closely with other engineers to test new functionality, reproduce reported issues, and refine features based on user needs, gaining hands-on experience with the full software development lifecycle.

Created Excel-based reports, presentations, and leadership updates to summarize event performance, budgets, and organizational activities, communicating progress, issues, and next steps clearly across different stakeholders.
